terms.gloss: lotus; in Pliny the water lily of the Nile, among several plants of the name
terms.comment: The Greek name, used by the Romans of several plants: the water lily of the Nile, the lotus tree of the Lotus-eaters, the nettle tree. Of the lotus of Asian ponds (Nelumbo nucifera) it is a modern use, as in the modern languages.

terms.gloss: the Egyptian bean, a great water plant of the Nile whose leaves served as cups
evidence: Verg. E. 4.20: mixtaque rīdentī colocāsia fundet acanthō
terms.comment: Pliny’s plant, also called cyamos, is commonly taken for the sacred lotus; Lewis & Short thinks Vergil’s may be the taro, and that Pliny confuses it with the water lily.

phrases.latin: In stāgnō lōtī flōrent; vidē quam magna folia!
phrases.english: The lotuses are blooming in the pond; look how big the leaves are!

phrases.latin: Folia lōtī aquam nōn retinent: guttae dēfluunt.
phrases.english: Lotus leaves don’t hold the water: the drops run off.
and the earth will pour out the Egyptian bean mingled with the smiling acanthus

sources: Lewis & Short: lotos · Lewis & Short: colocasia
